cities.name: Lytton
cities.note: Village ~90% destroyed in the 2021 Lytton Creek fire after a national heat record.

cities.name: Merritt
cities.note: Grassland–pine interface; Nicola valley winds and a single highway spine.

cities.name: Williams Lake
cities.note: 2017 Cariboo complex (Plateau, Hanceville) forced mass evacuations of the city.

nearby.name: 150 Mile House Fire-C20708- Central Area Command

cities.name: West Kelowna
cities.note: McDougall Creek 2023 crossed Okanagan Lake winds and destroyed hundreds of structures.

cities.name: Peachland
cities.note: Narrow lakeshore community with steep forested slopes above Highway 97.

cities.name: Penticton
cities.note: Sits between two lakes with dry Interior Douglas-fir slopes on three sides.

cities.name: Lake Country
cities.note: North of Kelowna along wooded benches and rural acreages.

cities.name: Oliver
cities.note: Canada’s driest inhabited valley; grass and sage ember risk on the benches.

cities.name: Kelowna
cities.note: Largest Okanagan city; interface benches and lake-effect winds drive ember attack.

cities.name: Ashcroft
cities.note: Elephant Hill 2017 started nearby and ran through the Thompson basin.

cities.name: Hope
cities.note: Canyon mouth; Mine Creek and Fraser Canyon fires periodically close Highway 1/3/5.

cities.name: Summerland
cities.note: Ponderosa–grass interface wrapping orchard benches.

cities.name: Port Alberni
cities.note: Cameron Bluffs 2023 cut Highway 4 to Tofino/Ucluelet for weeks.

cities.name: Invermere
cities.note: Wind-prone Columbia Valley interface; recreation and grass fire risk.

cities.name: Vernon
cities.note: Common evacuation staging point; grassland and timber interface to the west.

cities.name: Osoyoos
cities.note: Desert–vineyard interface against steep east and west slopes.

cities.name: Kamloops
cities.note: Regional hub; Sparks Lake 2021 and Elephant Hill 2017 burned on the west approaches.

cities.name: Fort St. John
cities.note: Donnie Creek 2023, the largest fire in B.C. record, burned to the northwest.

cities.name: 100 Mile House
cities.note: South Cariboo highway town ringed by Interior lodgepole and grassland.

cities.name: Cranbrook
cities.note: East Kootenay hub; dry valley bottom with timbered benches and frequent campfire starts.

cities.name: Lillooet
cities.note: McKay Creek 2021 and canyon winds; steep terrain limits engine access.

cities.name: Pemberton
cities.note: Valley agriculture against steep timber; limited highway options during closures.

cities.name: Burns Lake
cities.note: Lakes District town inside 2018 Nadina / Shovel Lake country.

cities.name: Castlegar
cities.note: Southeast Fire Centre city at the Columbia–Kootenay confluence.

cities.name: Kimberley
cities.note: Mountain resort town with forested subdivisions climbing the slopes.

cities.name: Cache Creek
cities.note: Highway 1 / 97 junction; repeated alerts from Elephant Hill and later complexes.

cities.name: Chetwynd
cities.note: Pine River valley town on the approach to Donnie Creek country.

cities.name: Boston Bar
cities.note: Linear canyon settlement with one-highway egress, repeatedly isolated by fire.

cities.name: Nelson
cities.note: Lakeside city climbing forested slopes; narrow roads in hillside neighbourhoods.

cities.name: Sicamous
cities.note: Highway 1 pinch-point with limited egress during Shuswap complex fires.

cities.name: Grand Forks
cities.note: Boundary dry-belt town; grassland and timber mix with valley winds.

cities.name: Vanderhoof
cities.note: 2018 Shovel Lake and related complexes burned heavily to the west.

cities.name: Quesnel
cities.note: North Cariboo mill town; 2017–18 and 2024–25 seasons pressed the timber supply.

cities.name: Smithers
cities.note: Northwest Fire Centre hub; Bulkley Valley interface on valley benches.

cities.name: Chilliwack
cities.note: Eastern Fraser Valley interface into Chilliwack River Valley and forested benches.

cities.name: Nanaimo
cities.note: Coastal Fire Centre city; west-slope interface into regional park forests.

cities.name: Golden
cities.note: Mountain highway town; limited egress if Trans-Canada or Highway 95 close.

cities.name: Princeton
cities.note: Highway 3 mountain town with pine beetle–killed stands on surrounding ridges.

cities.name: Squamish
cities.note: Corridor town under Howe Sound slopes; Sea-to-Sky is a single egress south/north.

cities.name: Salmon Arm
cities.note: Bush Creek East 2023 destroyed homes at Scotch Creek / Adams Lake nearby.

cities.name: Fort Nelson
cities.note: Boreal town; 2023–25 lightning megafires to the south and west (Nogah, Hossitl).

nearby.name: 23 nautical miles N of Ft Nelson

cities.name: Logan Lake
cities.note: Small highland town in a heavily burned 2021 landscape.

cities.name: Trail
cities.note: Industrial valley town; steep side-hills and limited river-crossing egress.

cities.name: Barriere
cities.note: North of Kamloops; 2021 Sparks Lake / Tremont landscape to the south-west.

cities.name: Houston
cities.note: Highway 16 community in a lightning-prone plateau forest.

cities.name: Dawson Creek
cities.note: Peace farmland–boreal edge; industrial and lightning starts on the plains.

cities.name: Terrace
cities.note: Skeena corridor; wetter climate but steep valley slash and railway/industrial starts.

cities.name: Clearwater
cities.note: North Thompson highway town; Wells Gray country with summer recreation ignitions.

cities.name: Revelstoke
cities.note: Valley bottom under steep timber; railway and highway ignition sources.

cities.name: Whistler
cities.note: Resort municipality in a forested valley with peak-season population spikes.

cities.name: Mackenzie
cities.note: Single-road mill town; 2023 Omineca-side complexes to the west.

nearby.name: 15 km North of Powder King on the Hwy

cities.name: Sooke
cities.note: Western CRD interface; one highway east, forest and wind on three sides.

cities.name: Langford
cities.note: Fast-growing Westshore interface into Sooke Hills and the Sea to Sea Green Blue Belt.

cities.name: Campbell River
cities.note: North Island timber town; industrial and lightning starts in the Sayward forest.

nearby.name: N of Wolf River - MONITOR ONLY

cities.name: Prince George
cities.note: 2025: Prince George Fire Centre held ~80% of provincial area burned.

cities.name: Courtenay
cities.note: Comox Valley; west-slope forest interface toward Forbidden Plateau.

nearby.name: N of Wolf River - MONITOR ONLY

cities.name: Fort St. James
cities.note: Stuart Lake community near 2018 Tezzeron / Chutanli fires.

cities.name: Mission
cities.note: North-of-Fraser interface into Stave and Steelhead forest lands.

cities.name: Fernie
cities.note: Elk Valley; steep valley with one highway and heavy recreation use.

cities.name: Victoria
cities.note: Capital core is low risk; the regional interface sits in Langford, Highlands, Sooke and Saanich.

cities.name: North Vancouver
cities.note: North Shore wildland–urban interface; steep coastal forest above dense housing.

cities.name: Maple Ridge
cities.note: Urban–forest edge along the Golden Ears and northern rural lots.

cities.name: Tofino
cities.note: Single highway access; isolated in 2023 when Cameron Bluffs closed Highway 4.
